items.title: PostgreSQL 18.6/17.11/16.15/15.19/14.24 close 28 CVEs, eleven at CVSS 8.8 with RCE reachable by authenticated users
Breaking change in a minor release: output_plugin_libraries allowlist defaults to pgoutput+test_decoding, killing wal2json/decoderbufs/pglogical slots
Mandatory post-patch REINDEX for btree_gist over NaN floats and bit types, ltree >14,653 labels, plus a GIN reltuples repair
CVE-2026-18408 (8.8): psql \unrestrict backquote expansion means restoring an untrusted dump can execute code
CVE-2026-14663 (6.5): pgcrypto produced trivially-breakable output for blowfish/twofish/cast5/3des — decrypt and re-encrypt
CVE-2026-14672 (5.3): mock SCRAM secrets didn't match non-default scram_iterations, giving a username-enumeration oracle
Sources contradict on the fixed PG18 version — announcement says 18.6, the security matrix renders 18.5
Oracle July 2026 CPU carried 54 MySQL patches, 9 remotely exploitable without credentials
CockroachDB tenant-scoped client cert could bypass tenant-scope checks for cluster-wide RPC access, fixed in v26.1.7/26.1.8
MariaDB 10.6.28 GA; confirm you're past 10.6.27 for the wsrep_notify_cmd command injection (CVE-2026-49261, CVSS 10.0)

PG19 REPACK (CONCURRENTLY) brings in-core online table rewrite, making pg_repack/pg_squeeze optional
PG19 autovacuum gets a five-component scoring launcher plus parallel index vacuum and pg_stat_autovacuum_scores
PG19 disables JIT by default and moves TOAST compression from pglz to LZ4; eager aggregation and NOT IN anti-joins added
A 13-year-old cascading-standby bug fixed: archive-recovery fallback on a WAL segment boundary never reconnected
MySQL Innovation moves to CalVer with 26.7.0 GA alongside 9.7.2 and 8.4.11 LTS; next Innovation is 26.10.0
MySQL 26.7 Change Stream Applier, Thread Pool in Community Edition, and post-quantum hybrid key exchange on OpenSSL 3.5+
MySQL Group Replication comm stack default flips XCOM to MYSQL; all XCOM options deprecated with warnings
SQLite 3.53.4 is a pure bug-fix roll-up for the 3.53 line, no CVEs or format changes
Turso announces a Postgres implementation in Rust on the same VDBE core, explicitly 'compatible enough… but not really 100%'
PlanetScale on presenting 256 shards / 768 Postgres servers as one database at petabyte scale
Past 64 subtransactions per transaction, SLRU pressure makes new read replicas refuse connections
AlloyDB previews BM25 full-text indexes via pg_textsearch on PG 17/18, plus BigQuery-to-AlloyDB table sync
Azure Database for PostgreSQL is still on the June minor set — two security cycles behind core as of the Aug 13 release
Citus 14.2 ships stability fixes: shard-clone sequence re-ranging, orphaned local shard cleanup, EXPLAIN segfaults
PostgreSQL 14 reaches EOL 2026-11-12; 14.24 is its final minor release
pg-java, a virtual-thread-based JVM Postgres driver, offers an alternative to pgjdbc's blocking-socket design
pgBackRest 2.59.0 adds PG19 support ahead of beta testing with real backup/PITR paths
August server batch: 8.3.8 (23 CVEs), 8.0.29 (19), 7.0.40 (16) — headlined by CVE-2026-18691 at CVSS 9.0
CVE-2026-18691 (9.0): credential exposure during intra-cluster connection setup across every supported line — rotate keyfiles/x.509 after patching
MongoDB 8.2 hit EOL 31 Jul with 8.2.12 as its last patch — no 8.2 build exists for the August 9.0, permanently unpatched
CVE-2026-18697 (8.7): unauthenticated DoS via mongos aggregation input validation, reachable pre-auth
CVE-2026-18712 (7.2): Queryable Encryption maintenance operations can modify collections outside their authorization scope
CVE-2026-18692 (7.7): time-series bucket use-after-free with RCE potential, confined to 8.3.0–8.3.7
July batch recap: CVE-2026-13072 (9.2) memory corruption and CVE-2026-13059 (8.6) RBAC bypass
BI Connector ODBC CVE-2026-19001 (9.5 critical) and CVE-2026-19003 (8.4) buffer overflows, fixed in 1.4.9
Java driver CVE-2026-18710 (8.2): SOCKS5 proxy credentials written to logs in cleartext, fixed in 5.9.2
Compass CVE-2026-14881 (8.4): a crafted connection file overrides the OIDC browser-open command for arbitrary shell execution
Stricter compound-wildcard-index validation was backported into patch releases 8.2.4/8.0.18/7.0.29, so index-creation code can fail after a routine security patch
Cost-Based Ranker is now the default plan-selection backstop in 8.3 — capture explain baselines before upgrading
8.3 changes $facet memory errors to ExceededMemoryLimit, defaults 2dsphere to version 4, and adds day-of-week balancer windows
8.3.8 fixes three real WiredTiger bugs: in-memory page leaks, eviction-thread panic, and recovery silently discarding cleanup errors
8.0.28/8.0.29 fix checkpoint handles never resetting, reconciliation failing with 'Device or resource busy', and prefetch not enabling
8.0.29 rejects uncompressed time-series buckets over 200MB before insert and blocks converting viewless collections to capped
BSONColumn gets optimized count/first/last/min/max pushdown in 8.0.28, helping time-series aggregation on the LTS line
SERVER-125724: $scoreFusion silently ignored combination.expression, so hybrid-search relevance tuning was doing nothing for some configs
Percona Search for MongoDB tech preview ships a mongot distribution targeting MongoDB's Voyage-AI-only embedding restriction
Percona Server for MongoDB 8.3 tech preview lets WiredTiger cache size be set as a percentage of available memory
Percona Server for MongoDB 8.0.28-12 adds RHEL 10/Debian 13 and SBOM/VEX, but is based on 8.0.28 — one CVE cycle behind
Node driver 7.5.0 signals MongoDB 9.0 LTS and changes MongoClient.close() to close in-use connections on all servers
Atlas reverted the UI read preference back to primary after secondaryPreferred produced confusing stale reads
Atlas Search index-time sorting pre-sorts documents at index time, fixing $search + $sort blowups on large result sets
MongoDB claims 8.3 delivers +35% writes/+45% reads over 8.0; Percona claims up to +195% on time-series inserts — neither publishes methodology
Parquet Java 1.18.0 changes float column statistics to IEEE 754 total order with NaN counts, a pruning-semantics change across reader versions
Parquet Java 1.18.0 drops Java 8 from core modules and removes parquet-pig; Java 8 runtimes stop at 1.17.1
Parquet formalizes a major-version policy reserving majors for forward-incompatible changes; ALP encoding and a File logical type approved
Iceberg's definitive Variant write-up: shredding exists only in Parquet, and Flink 2.1 is unshredded-only
Iceberg v4 entered formal workstream scoping; relative paths and content stats ratified but no settable v4 spec today
Delta Lake 3.3.3 fixes metadata cleanup deleting transaction log files still needed for time travel and CDF inside the retention window
Delta Lake 4.3.1 fixes a CaseInsensitiveStringMap bug that lowercased oauth.clientId and broke Delta REST Catalog auth
Polaris 1.7.0 adds opt-in idempotency for createTable/updateTable — safe retry semantics at the REST-catalog layer
CVE-2026-64640 (low): Polaris register endpoint read attacker-chosen metadata before validating allowed locations, fixed in 1.7.0
Polaris 1.7.0 removes createTableDirectWithWriteDelegation and the admin bootstrap schema-version option
Unity Catalog OSS 0.5 ships the UC Delta API — versioned, intent-based atomic commits over REST with vended credentials
AWS Glue Data Catalog can now export metadata to S3 Tables in preview, a migration path off Glue-native tables
An Apache Iceberg Terraform provider reached v0.1.0 RC for managing namespaces, tables and grants as code
Trino 483 stops writing deletion vectors that other Delta readers reject — the highest-value interop fix of the month
Trino 483 requires s3.auth-type=IAM_ROLE when s3.iam-role is set and removes the web-identity provider, across Iceberg/Delta/Hudi/Hive
DataFusion Comet 1.0.0 ships after two years of incubation, including an Iceberg native-scan wrong-results fix
iceberg-rust 0.10.0 lands table encryption end-to-end with AES-GCM, streaming crypto and KMS integration
Debezium 3.6.1.Final masks all credential-bearing config properties and fixes three data-corruption bugs in Oracle, MySQL and the JDBC sink
Debezium 3.7.0.Alpha2 removes Oracle 12 continuous mining and the Cassandra 3 connector — both hard breaks
Debezium 3.7.0.Alpha1's MySQL JDBC-sink type audit turns previously-silent corruption into loud errors
dlt 1.30.0 adds cross-destination joins spanning duckdb, motherduck, ducklake and lance, plus retryable schema migrations
AWS MSK Express brokers can deliver Kafka data straight into Iceberg streaming tables without a Flink or Spark job
PyIceberg 0.12.0rc1 is on PyPI but drew a binding -1 over a correctness regression — stay on 0.11.1
Arrow 25.0.0 carries Iceberg Variant in memory via the canonical extension type arrow.parquet.variant
DuckDB 1.5.5 fixes swapped min/max for 128-bit DECIMAL in RETURN_STATS — a statistics correctness bug affecting pruning
Iceberg 1.12.0 branch cut is on or after Aug 26; fixes must land before then
CVE-2026-47040: Oracle Net Services at CVSS 9.1, remotely exploitable without authentication, fixed in the July RU
CVE-2026-61211: RDBMS/DBMS_CLOUD flaw at CVSS 9.9, affects 19.3-19.31 and 23.4-23.26.2, fix available
CVE-2026-47046 (8.2) and CVE-2026-7383 (8.1) are 23ai/26ai-exclusive — moving to the newest codeline shifts CVE exposure rather than shrinking it
CVE-2026-47045/47060/47061 affect JDBC and client-only installs; patching the server does not close them
July 2026 CPU shipped 15 Database Server patches, 6 remotely exploitable without auth, inside a ~1,400-CVE advisory
Oracle security events are now monthly, not quarterly: next CSPU 18 Aug, next full CPU 20 Oct — eight CSPUs plus four CPUs a year
Oracle pre-announced the July RU a week early with a readiness checklist, citing AI-accelerated exploit development (MOS PNEWS3015)
19.32 patch numbers: DB RU 39472050, GI RU 39467003, OJVM RU 39222882 — verify against MOS 888.1 before staging
E-Business Suite 12.2 is certified with 19.32 on Linux, removing the usual EBS blocker for prompt security patching
Exadata System Software 25.1.19.0.0 is the final update on the 25.1 branch — no further fixes, security or otherwise
Exadata System Software 26.1.1.0.0, 25.2.12.0.0 (recommended) and 25.1.19.0.0 (final), with patch numbers published
RU 23.26.3 adds log-buffer-based auto redo prioritization and PDB target redo generation management — the first real lever for noisy-PDB log file sync
RU 23.26.3 adds transport-lag-based auto redo prioritization for Data Guard SYNC/FASTSYNC topologies
Scalar quantization for distributed HNSW indexes cuts memory and disk footprint across RAC instances — verify recall on your own embeddings
RU 23.26.3 gives JSON-Relational Duality Views array limits, deletable shared tables and user-defined identifying keys
RU 23.26.3 adds Intelligent Drain Timing and MAA Client Readiness, targeting the connection-draining path during planned maintenance
RU 23.26.3 adds Oracle AI Database as a Redis Server, DATEADD, and Unicode 17.0
ADB Serverless adds retry_params for DBMS_CLOUD.SEND_REQUEST — per-call HTTP retry control for flaky pipeline endpoints
ADB Serverless GET_DEFINITION returns executable PL/SQL for DBMS_CLOUD, DBMS_CLOUD_AI and pipeline objects, enabling source control
ADB Serverless adds AS OF TIMESTAMP time travel for Apache Iceberg external tables via Databricks, Glue or Hadoop Catalog
ADB Serverless Select AI adds a Supervisor Agent pattern, managed MCP and A2A servers, and IMPORT_TEAM/EXPORT_TEAM versioning
ADB Dedicated adds cross-tenancy OCI Vault customer-managed keys — provision-time only, existing ACDs unsupported
Exadata Exascale PDB thin clones consume effectively no storage until written, with clones-of-clones and upstream-recreate survival
Exadata VM live migration moves OS/memory state between KVM hosts with storage on Exascale, under strict same-generation constraints
Nothing on the optimizer, In-Memory, Smart Scan or AWR/ASH published in the window; the Optimizer blog's last substantive post is Dec 2025
python-oracledb 4.0.2 is a bug-fix release on the 4.0 line, which added thin-mode CQN and AQ notifications
Oracle Database 23ai is now Oracle AI Database 26ai with docs moved to /oracle-database/26/ paths, breaking bookmarks and scrapers
Bundle 2026_06 is scheduled to auto-enable in an unspecified August release, carrying 18 changes including three High-impact items
BCR-2359: plural INTERVAL qualifiers now parse as units — INTERVAL '3' days changes from 3 seconds to 3 days, silently
BCR-2376: CORTEX_ENABLED_CROSS_REGION auto-sets to a geography default — set it to DISABLED explicitly if you have residency constraints
BCR-2362: dbt project objects collapse to a single mutable 'live' version, breaking versioned snow://dbt paths and SET DEFAULT_VERSION
BCR-2373: QAS auto-enables on all new standard warehouses at scale factor 8, up from Gen2/multi-cluster only at factor 2
Bundle 2026_05 went enabled-by-default, making managed Iceberg tables replicate by default in replication and failover groups
MFA Milestone 3 is running now on a rolling per-account basis: all non-human password auth blocked, LEGACY_SERVICE auto-migrated, no bundle opt-out
Adaptive Warehouses are GA with per-query billing; QAS usage folds into compute credits so existing QAS dashboards read zero
Gen2 is now the default warehouse generation, so a September-created warehouse is Gen2 + QAS@8 by default
ADAPTIVE refresh mode is GA and is now Snowflake's recommended mode for all incremental workloads — not applied retroactively
CUSTOM_INCREMENTAL dynamic tables are GA, the sanctioned exit from streams-and-tasks for CDC with deletes and stream-static joins
CREATE OR ALTER DYNAMIC TABLE is GA and extended to dynamic Iceberg tables, removing drop-and-recreate logic
Four more DT capabilities GA in one week: VOLATILE scalar UDFs in incremental refresh, DML into frozen regions, pass-through policies, multi-DT refresh
Openflow Connector for SQL Server CDC is GA with initial snapshot, incremental sync and automatic schema evolution
Amazon S3 Tables Iceberg REST catalog integration is GA with no Glue required, plus outbound private connectivity
Inline Stored Procedures for hybrid tables enter preview, executing atomically at the query-processing layer for OLTP-style writes
SERVICE_AGENT user type is GA — a non-interactive agent identity with workload identity federation including SPIFFE/SPIRE
ACCESS_HISTORY gains agents_info and QUERY_HISTORY gains agent_type, so agent-issued SQL is finally attributable
Cost anomaly alerts can now route to Slack/SMS/webhook at account and org level
Per-user AI spend quotas enter preview with monthly and daily credit caps and automatic blocking at threshold
String/binary session variables go from 256 bytes to 16KB and object definitions from 95KB to 1MB
Multi-Party Approval is GA, with tag-based data protection policies and OIDC federated authentication in preview
.NET driver 6.0.0 is a major version bump — assume breaking changes until you read the changelog
Gen2 perf-vs-cost claims don't reconcile: ~30-40% faster on TPCH-1000 but Flexera puts Gen2 credit rates 25-35% above Gen1
No new Snowflake CVEs in the window; the most recent bulletin remains CVE-2026-6442 from April
DBR 13.3 LTS reaches end of support Aug 22 and received neither the July nor August maintenance round
Databricks CLI bundle deployments default to the direct engine Aug 26, with the Terraform engine removed from new releases in September

Arrow-optimized Python UDFs are on by default in DBR 19 and Spark 4.2, changing type-coercion behavior, not just performance
Automatic upgrades began pushing row tracking and Checkpoint V2 onto existing UC managed tables, with catalog commits and deletion vectors in August
MANAGE no longer requires USE CATALOG/USE SCHEMA, which silently activated previously dormant broad grants
Sept 14: workspace entitlement inheritance from the users system group is enforced off, and SCIM prune can strip everyone's entitlements
Delta Lake 4.3.0 errors on MERGE INTO against empty-schema targets and reports physical recordCount on UniForm+DV Iceberg tables
All Lakebase Provisioned instances are force-upgraded to Autoscaling with new regional connection strings; the Provisioned UI disappears Sept 1
DBR 18 and 18 ML transitioned to LTS, and DBR moves to a unified release model where pinning a version no longer pins behavior
Two maintenance rounds carry correctness fixes: windowed min/max wrong on BinaryType, MERGE source checksum verification, an ArrowDeserializers data race
Apache Spark 4.2.0 shipped with ~1,700 JIRAs, native GEOMETRY/GEOGRAPHY, a SQL CHANGES clause, QUALIFY and NEAREST BY
Variant and Variant shredding are GA, auto-enabling on new tables from DBR 17.3 — but stats collection needs DBR 18.1+
Multi-statement transactions are GA on UC managed Delta tables, requiring catalog commits on every participating table
Delta Sharing of tables with deletion vectors or column mapping is GA, retiring duplicate no-DV copies
OpenSharing SecureConnect is GA, and planned billing changes will charge recipients for public cross-region connectivity
Change data feed on materialized views enters beta; MVs use automatic CDF so feeds appear without per-table config
REPLACE USING flows enter beta, closing the partial-snapshot gap with key-based replacement and SEQUENCE BY ordering
READ METADATA privilege is GA, giving auditors grant and policy visibility without granting MANAGE
Secrets in Unity Catalog are GA with a three-level namespace, providing a migration path off workspace-scoped scopes
RBAC entered public preview letting users assume a role rather than accumulate grants; ABAC GRANT policies expanded to MCP, agent and skill services
Unity AI Gateway is GA and all Databricks-managed MCP connectors migrated to it — users must reauthenticate or connectors break
ai_search() enters beta, fanning a natural-language query across indexes with dedupe, rerank and grounded synthesis in SQL
New cross-region and public-internet egress charges apply to all customers on Lakebase, SecureConnect, Zerobus and Files API
Genie pricing changed three times in five weeks, with correction records pushed into system.billing.usage to net prior charges to zero
Alert system tables enter preview and MV/ST refreshes now inherit warehouse tags for cost attribution
DBSQL release notes have gone stale — the index reports channel 2026.20 while the detail page stops at Jun 30
Databricks' Liquid Clustering claims (35% lower clustering time, 2.5x faster than Z-order) are vendor-run on vendor-chosen layouts
Fluid scaling autoscaler is GA with per-second billing and no one-minute minimum, opt-in per reservation, claimed up to 34% cost reduction
History-based optimization is GA: up to 50% lower P90 execution time and 15% lower slot usage, applied automatically with no DDL
Advanced runtime is GA with enhanced vectorization, claimed up to 10x speedup and 40% slot-time reduction on native and Iceberg tables
Short query optimization is GA: up to 10x lower slot usage, sub-second P99 and 3x throughput for high-concurrency BI traffic
Project caps enter preview to cap max slots and concurrency per project inside a reservation, admission-time only
Iceberg managed tables get partitioning, multi-statement transactions and advanced runtime at GA, claimed 2x vs self-managed Iceberg
Data Transfer Service adds Iceberg managed tables as a destination in preview, from GCS, S3 and Azure Blob
DTS PostgreSQL and MySQL connectors reach GA, SQL Server enters preview, and the Snowflake migration connector is GA
APPENDS and CHANGES change-history table functions are GA, offering a SQL-native alternative to bolt-on CDC tables
Storage Write API nomenclature changed: legacy insertAll is now 'REST' and the old Storage Write API is now 'gRPC'
Cross-cloud Lakehouse renamed borderless Lakehouse, and the product absorbed the BigLake naming
Snowflake as a remote catalog provider for federated queries enters preview, with SAP BDC federation alongside
CVE-2026-14934 (9.4 critical): missing authorization in BigQuery, Dataform and Colab Enterprise repositories, patched server-side May 10
Data governance tags enter preview for column-level security and dynamic data masking via tags, parallel to Dataplex policy tags
Google ships its own first-party ODBC driver for BigQuery at GA as an alternative to Simba, with no feature comparison published
google-cloud-bigquery 3.43.0 and 3.42.3 fix socket leaks and raise floors to Python 3.10 and protobuf 6.33.5
bigframes 2.48.0 silently changes GeminiTextGenerator's default model to gemini-2.5-flash, a behavior and cost change
BigQuery DTS billing label changed case on Aug 11, silently zeroing any cost-attribution query filtering on the uppercase literal
Legacy SQL restrictions took effect after June 1: projects with no legacy-SQL usage in the prior window have it disabled
ALTER SEARCH INDEX DDL enters preview, allowing in-place index reconfiguration instead of drop-and-rebuild
BigQuery release notes published nothing from July 30 to Aug 14 while major announcements landed on the Cloud blog
HBO, advanced runtime and SQO all apply automatically, so identical SQL now costs different slot-hours depending on execution history
Redshift Serverless begins enforcing KMS key permission checks after Aug 17 — restore and CreateWorkgroup calls fail without direct kms permissions
TLS 1.2 minimum is enforced on provisioned and Serverless from Aug 30; TLS 1.0/1.1 connections are rejected

Late-binding view parsing moves to the consumer cluster in P204, removing a producer-side bottleneck for data sharing fan-out
Queries referencing user temporary tables can now run on concurrency scaling clusters, a long-standing ELT staging exclusion
Patch 203 makes ANALYZE up to 30% faster and widens automatic DISTKEY assignment to COPY-from-Spectrum and explicitly-encoded tables

rg.large and rg.12xlarge reached GA across 28 regions, the trailing track, and GovCloud, completing the Graviton RG ladder
AWS published a DC2-to-RG upgrade playbook with node-mapping ratios and three migration paths — but no DC2 end-of-support date
AUTO_REMEDIATION for zero-ETL databases automatically resynchronizes tables that hit replication issues
Two new CloudWatch metrics expose zero-ETL replication lag as an alarmable gap without polling system views
DynamoDB zero-ETL now honors ACCEPTINVCHARS and TRUNCATECOLUMNS so invalid UTF-8 no longer stalls replication

Data API adds long polling, ListSessions and non-atomic batch execution, cutting API call volume and Lambda duration
ODBC 1.x driver end of support moves to Sept 30, extended from the original June 30 date
Python UDF enforcement began with P203; all Python UDF support ended after June 30 — migrate to Lambda UDFs
CVE-2026-8178: RCE via unsafe class loading in the Redshift JDBC driver before 2.2.2; CVE-2026-8838 affects the Python driver ≤2.1.13
Three-year All Upfront Serverless Reservations offer up to 50% off on-demand, managed at payer-account level
AWS published a multi-Region DR reference architecture using existing primitives, with costed RPO/RTO comparisons
MV auto-refresh behavior has diverged between Serverless and provisioned and the docs contradict each other
RG is becoming the default tier and every performance claim is now benchmarked against RA3, which is the new legacy
Fabric Data Warehouse moved to vNode-based CU metering with a one-minute allocation floor, penalizing many-small-query workloads
GPU Query acceleration preview bills at 3.446 CU per core vs 0.538, applies to every warehouse in the workspace, and cancels in-flight queries on toggle
The Warehouse metering change has no publicly stated effective date; docs describe vNode allocation as if it were always the model
New SQL analytics endpoint metadata sync enters preview with on-demand refresh triggered by a stale read
Usage-based resource estimations are GA, feeding prior execution cardinalities back into resource requests
Custom SQL pools enter preview with up to 8 pools per workspace classified by application name or regex
Fabric Runtime 2.0 is GA with Spark 4.1, Delta 4.2, Python 3.13 and Java 21, becoming the default in late September

OneLake storage tiers and lifecycle management are GA; reading 1TB from cold costs ~665,000 CU-seconds vs 2,600 from hot

On-prem gateways older than the June 2026 release now consume CUs for Oracle and SQL Server mirroring OneLake transactions

RTI had a heavy GA month: Real-Time Dashboard, Eventhouse folders, update policies joining accelerated shortcuts, mTLS connectors
Fabric mirroring GA list widens to Snowflake, Oracle, SAP and Databricks metadata; default retention is 1 day for newer items
CVE-2026-58647: Power BI Report Server XSS/spoofing, with NVD scoring 5.4 Medium against Microsoft's 8.0 High
The Synapse 1 Aug 2026 trusted-services retirement did not happen — it slipped to 1 June 2027 with a new workspace setting by March 2027
Synapse Spark runtimes 3.3 and 3.4 are unsupported and deprecated with no security fixes — the real deadline, not a service EOL
Fabric known issues moved off Microsoft Learn and the release plan moved to roadmap.fabric.microsoft.com, breaking deep links
ClickHouse 26.7 lands with a long backward-incompatible list including S3 credential resolution and glob matching changes
S3 server credentials no longer resolve implicitly inside user SQL — explicit creds or NOSIGN required for table functions and named collections
ClickHouse 26.7 refuses to start if insert_deduplication_version still carries a legacy value — a plan-your-upgrade item

Runtime filters can now prune granules via the primary key and skip indexes, with hash join using compact 8-byte row references

ClickHouse LTS rollups v26.3.17.110-lts and v25.8.29.51-lts shipped, so 25.8 LTS still receives backports
ClickHouse Cloud previews sticky replica routing via session_id, keeping session objects and a warm page cache
StarRocks 4.0.14 disables unsafe Zone Map pruning on division expressions and changes GIN NOT MATCH null semantics

StarRocks 4.0.13 changed LIKE escape handling to match MySQL 8 — a semantics change, not a bug fix
CelerData rebranded to PhoenixAI with an $80M Series B; celerdata.com and docs now redirect to phoenixdata.ai
Doris 4.0.8 flips the Nereids distribute planner on by default on upgrade — a plan-shape change in a patch release
Doris 4.0.8 requires explicit enablement and auth on the BE _stream_load_forward endpoint, reading like a real exposure being closed
Doris 4.1.3 adds Python UDF/UDAF/UDTF and an ANN TopN small-candidate brute-force fallback that fixes the recall cliff
DuckDB 1.5.5 patches metadata corruption from DROP COLUMN, hash-aggregate segfaults and decimal min/max wrong across row groups

Trino 483 makes the redesigned Web UI default at /ui and disables the legacy UI by default
Trino 483 fixes NOT BETWEEN and right/full outer join correctness bugs, and adds PIVOT, OVERLAPS and JSON accessor syntax
Dremio 26.1.9/26.1.10 fix Iceberg equality-delete stale data and MAX/MIN wrong results on VARCHAR columns over 16 chars
Databend nightlies reached v1.2.932 with a fused TopN operator carrying runtime scan filters
Pinot 1.6.0 constrains rolling-upgrade order — brokers must be at least as new as servers — and MV aggregations now return SQL NULL
Pinot 1.6.0 removes deprecated endpoints, rejects TimeFieldSpec in schema validation and tightens the index SPI
Managed-layer differentiation is drifting from query speed toward governance, multi-tenancy and agent integration
Apache Druid shipped nothing in the window; Firebolt, SingleStore, Teradata and VeloDB had no verifiable releases
AMD EPYC 9006 Venice launched with 16 memory channels, 1.6 TB/s per socket, 128 PCIe Gen6 lanes and CXL 3.1
